analysis.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. AI_Literacies: Artists who are using vGenAI need more knowledge and resources that can inform the critical use of these tools.
Generative_KI: In this paper, we critically analyze Stable Diffusion (SD), a widely used open-source vGenAI tool, through visual and intersectional analysis.
Prompting: When it came to the visual images, we used a specific prompting strategy to produce a dataset comprising 180 images using SDXL.
By keeping prompts minimal, we aimed to observe the default outputs and hegemonic aesthetics in the imagery.
Bias_Ungleichheit: We demonstrate how imagery produced through SD perpetuates pre-existing power systems such as sexism, racism, heteronormativity, and ableism, and assumes a default individual as white, able-bodied, and masculine-presenting.
Gender: Across various images, gender assignments were automatically applied by SDXL, resulting in aesthetics that excluded feminine or non-binary representations.
Diversitaet: Consequently, unless specifically prompted for diversity, the AI-generated imagery lacks diversity to a significant extent, perpetuating ableist norms by portraying stereotypical bodies with uniform characteristics as the visual standard
Feministisch: Our methodological approach draws primarily from feminist Science and Technology Studies (STS)

analysis.AN_Notes: Qualitative interpretative visual analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from minimal prompts along privilege and disadvantage, ideology and everyday scenarios, followed by a micro, meso and macro intersectional analysis. Prompting is the research instrument; the only prompting recommendation is that users be more conscious of what kind of prompts they use, with no codable technique (AN_Prompt_Techniques None). Religion was deliberately excluded from the prompts and is not coded. Harm types from the work's own image analysis: Stereotyping (darker skin tones tied to criminality, own named harm), Exclusionary_Norms (white, able-bodied, heteronormative masculine default), Erasure (absence of non-binary and disabled representations), Misrepresentation (reductionist portrayal of cultural contexts, Global South shown only as impoverished). The less accurate depiction of dishes such as fufu concerns cultural items rather than a quality difference between social groups and is not coded as Disparate_Performance. Gender definition Explicit rests on footnote 2, which determines the binary gender norm and replaces man and woman by heteronormative feminine and masculine representations. Mitigation: better training data curation, more conscious prompting by users, regulation, criminal culpability, team diversity and algorithmic reparation, all proposed. AN_Task None: the work audits a general image generator without an application task of professional practice.

AN_Gender_Definition.quote: By simplistically interpreting the images using terms such as 'man' and 'woman', we are at danger of reinforcing the binary gender norm (the assumption that people of a certain gender should be associated with a certain set of visual features).

AN_Gender_Understanding.quote: Power systems are essentially beliefs, cultural norms, and practices (Guillaumin 2002) that reinforce certain ideologies, such as heteronormativity, patriarchy, racism, and ableism.
Furthermore, non-binary gender representations were absent due to the strong binary gender aesthetics

AN_Theory_Reference.quote: Our intersectional approach builds on Sharma et al. (2023)'s analytical framework, which encompasses 3 key lenses of intersectionality: (1) the micro (individual) lens; (2) the meso (institutional) lens; and the macro (power systems) lens.

AN_Theory_Reference.theory: Feminist Science and Technology Studies and feminist visual cultural studies
